blocks.html:
What to know

  • Sickle cell disease is a folding disease. A single glutamate-to-valine change in the beta-globin chain creates a sticky patch; deoxygenated hemoglobin polymerizes and distorts the red cell.
  • Enzymes are diagnostic markers. Alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase rise with liver injury; alkaline phosphatase rises with bile-duct or bone disease; creatine kinase rises after muscle damage.
  • Monoclonal antibodies are targeted proteins. They bind one epitope and are used in cancer therapy, autoimmune disease, and laboratory tests.
  • Protein therapeutics must be handled carefully. Insulin, growth hormone, and monoclonal antibodies are digested if swallowed, so most are injected; formulation and storage protect their shape.
  • Proteomics and mass spectrometry identify proteins and post-translational modifications, linking a patient sample to a molecular diagnosis.

Check

check.question: Sickle cell disease results from which change?

options.text: A single amino-acid substitution in beta-globin
Loss of the entire beta-globin gene
An antibody against red blood cells

check.explanation: The classic mutation is glutamate to valine at position 6 of beta-globin. One residue changes the surface, and the polymerized protein changes the cell shape.
